_about: The ElevenLabs voices a voiceover may be read in, and the only place a voice id for one is kept (his own clone's id is also in krish-clone's registry, which wins; scripts/velib/voice_bank.py refuses a bank whose krish entry disagrees with it). Krish, 2026-11-17: "for all voiceovers and carousels, I want there to either be an audio track over the carousel, or, if it's a voiceover, then I want Eleven Labs voices used to do the voiceovers. I always want to be given a few options in my control center. We should have some stock voices approved in Eleven Labs and, obviously, my own Krish remix voice too as an option on the control center Content Board. voiceovers would have light approved epidemic audio behind the voice." Each voice pins its own ElevenLabs model (model): a voice is generated on it and nothing else. Every voice id was read from ElevenLabs (creative_list_voices, 2026-11-17), never typed from memory. A stock voice is proposed until his press on the Content Board approves it for the bank; only an approved voice is generated (ve voice clone --voice), and the board offers proposed ones marked as proposed so he can hear them. preview_url is ElevenLabs' own free preview clip (no credits spent); the board plays it through GET /api/board/sign-offs?voice=<id>. The words of a sample are never his script: a preview is ElevenLabs' own line. whole_script says whether a voice has held on a whole script: a voice is tested on a whole script before a voiceover in it reaches him, and the board says when it has not.
ruling: Krish, 2026-11-17 (typed in a Claude session): for all voiceovers, ElevenLabs voices, a few options on the Content Board, some approved stock voices and his own Krish Remix voice; voiceovers have light approved Epidemic audio behind the voice; carousels carry an approved audio track

voices.name: Krish v2
voices.line: His own voice: a Voice Remix of Krish Remix, "Same man, same accent and tone. Softer, glottal T's like relaxed London speech" (its ElevenLabs description).
voices.why: His best narration voice so far (Krish, 2026-11-17: "yes, 15% is right, go ahead - ensure the krish-clone repo and the other two sessions know that this is the best choice thus far in terms of voice ID and your usage of it", relayed by the voice-design session).
voices.model_why: eleven_v3, never v4: on v4 his voice did not sound like itself (Krish, 2026-11-17: "v3 sounds right").
voices.speed_how: The chosen take is sped up 15% keeping pitch (ffmpeg atempo=1.15) after generation: the v3 settings have no speed control. ve voice clone does it when it makes the .wav.
voices.delivery: eleven_v3 audio tags before the beats ([excited] on the hook, [casual], [playful] on the turn, [conversational] on the explanation); his approved words unchanged. Render two takes and keep the better.
voices.approval_source: krish-clone config/synthetic-approvals.json, entry krish-voice-elevenlabs-v2 (krishanraja/krish-clone PR #13; generation is refused until it is on main)

whole_script.note: Held his voice for a ten-second opening only; on the full 90-second script it drifted to an accent he does not have, at Natural and at Robust stability, as one generation and paragraph by paragraph (the Tue 17 habits voiceover session; every generation id in krish-clone docs/GENERATORS.md, krish-clone PR #14). He recorded that piece himself.

voices.name: Krish Remix (backup)
voices.line: His own ElevenLabs voice: "more of a posh london accent with an aussie twang" (its ElevenLabs description).
voices.why: His first ElevenLabs voice, the registry voice krish-voice-elevenlabs (15 Nov 2026); kept approved as the backup since Krish v2 (17 Nov).
voices.model_why: Krish, 2026-11-17, after hearing the same lines on eleven_v4, eleven_v3 and eleven_multilingual_v2 (relayed by the Tuesday habits voiceover session): "v3 sounds right". On eleven_v4 he asked "Why does this not sound like that Krish Remix voice when I play it in ElevenLabs?"
voices.delivery: eleven_v3 audio tags ([excited], [casual], [playful], [conversational]) give the more animated delivery he approved; the words stay exactly as signed.
